clue.text: Beauty treatment? Female having a cold one gets a line reduced

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: reduced means the word line is cut down to just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A woman with a cold finds her queue at the salon has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts 'line' down to its first letter, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A face-cleansing and massage session at a salon is a standard beauty treatment; the question mark flags the misleading surface.

clue.text: Fine performance conveys reality

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A fine stage show carries a sense of the real world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true or actual is a matter of reality, a synonym in the sense of what is the case.

clue.text: Smoked heroin — what George did?

definitions.meaning: slang for inhaling the fumes of heated heroin
Saint George pursued and slew a dragon in legend

explanation.surface: A drug habit set against the legend of England's patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for inhaling heated heroin fumes, also literally Saint George's pursuit of the legendary beast.

clue.text: An isolated person engaging male hospital official

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the solitary person's word holds another inside it

parts.note: a loner keeps away from others

explanation.surface: A solitary figure hires a man as an administrator at the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: An ALMONER was a hospital social worker in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was a British hospital social worker handling patients' welfare, so a hospital official.

clue.text: Produce chaps not primarily wanting sex

indicators.note: not primarily says the first letter of the word for chaps is dropped

parts.note: chaps are men
gender is a synonym for sex

explanation.surface: Men who, at first, are not after sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not primarily' removes the first letter of MEN, leaving EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or give rise to something, a verb synonym as in feelings that are created.

clue.text: Only some given a talent at birth

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a few people are born gifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the time of being born, as in prenatal and postnatal care.

clue.text: Groups with members one over the eight — and seen to be drunk

definitions.text: Groups with members one over the eight

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters of the two words are rearranged, like a staggering drinker

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinking groups who have had one too many are spotted tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British phrase for being tipsy, but here it literally means nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets of nine, from the Greek for nine; one over eight members makes nine.

clue.text: Prepare for evening in to sketch out part of new decor?

definitions.meaning: closing the window drapes before a night at home

definitions.text: sketch out part of new decor?
definitions.meaning: making a drawing of the window hangings when planning a room

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a night in, or designing the soft furnishings of a redecorated room.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for pulling drapes closed at dusk, read literally as drawing a picture of the window hangings.

clue.text: After Bible lessons maybe thought to be saved

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject that may include Bible lessons
deemed means thought or judged

explanation.surface: Someone after Bible study thinks they have been saved.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian language a soul delivered from sin has been rescued, the theological sense of the word.

clue.text: Delights of small children and their embracers?

parts.note: CH is a short form of children
arms are what hug and embrace

explanation.surface: The joys of little ones and the people who cuddle them.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to delight someone is to enchant or captivate them.

clue.text: Principle right for small boy and father to hold

parts.note: Stan is a shortened form of the boy's name Stanley

indicators.note: to hold means the father's word contains another piece

parts.note: dad is father

explanation.surface: A rule that a little lad and his dad should keep to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small boy' is a shortened boy's name: Stan, from Stanley.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark or norm of conduct, as in moral standards, is a principle.

clue.text: Useless bit of drudgery complete

parts.note: fag is British slang for tedious work
to end is to complete or finish

explanation.surface: Finishing off a pointless scrap of tiresome work.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is British slang for a chore; a fag end is also a cigarette stub.
explanation.definitionFit: The leftover remnant of anything, like a cigarette stub, is a worthless scrap.

clue.text: A learner just getting excited about the old man who was a philosopher?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the father
excited signals the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
pa is a name for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: A student gets worked up about their father, the would-be thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting excited' signals the anagram and 'about' the container; the question mark admits the surface's student is only a would-be thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist thinker who wrote Being and Nothingness was a leading twentieth-century philosopher.

clue.text: Course officials at Aintree, say

definitions.meaning: the first course of a meal, plural in form but naming one course
officials who set horse races going; Aintree is a racecourse near Liverpool

explanation.surface: The racecourse officials at the Grand National meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers form the opening dish of a meal; race officials who start races also bear this title.

clue.text: Broadcasting jazz music when leader of orchestra has come in

indicators.note: has come in places the letter inside the jazz word

parts.note: swing is a style of big-band jazz

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of orchestra

explanation.surface: A jazz piece going out on air once the bandleader arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting originally meant scattering seed widely by hand, a farming synonym for planting.

clue.text: What's observed in the auditorium?

indicators.note: an auditorium is where audiences hear things, so it signals a homophone

parts.note: what is observed has been seen

explanation.surface: What a theatre audience watches.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a stage set is what an audience watches.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting on stage, or one part of a play, is what an audience watches from its seats.

clue.text: Female companion joining male, an abettor in crime?

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A woman friend teams up with a man in an accomplice's role.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster's loyal follower or heavy is an accomplice who helps with wrongdoing.

clue.text: Improve as journalist, enthralling about half the adult population?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the journalist's letters surround the rest

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
men make up roughly half of grown-ups

explanation.surface: An editor improving copy while captivating half of all grown-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or polish a text is to make it better, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Get into a really good habit?

definitions.text: Get into a really good habit?

parts.words: Get into a really good habit?
parts.note: habit here is clothing, as a nun's habit; putting on fine clothes is the joke

explanation.surface: Advice on adopting a beneficial routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means a garment, so the phrase is about donning smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on smart or fancy clothing is literally getting into a fine outfit.

clue.text: Heavy rain has river flooding county and old city

indicators.note: flooding means pouring into, so the river goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A deluge sends a river over the land of a county and an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is a county in Northern Ireland; 'flooding' puts the river into the middle of the combined pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrential burst of precipitation is a sudden heavy fall of water from the sky.

clue.text: Fit out with material, trim all around

indicators.note: all around means the trim word surrounds the fabric

parts.note: to pare is to trim
rep is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: A tailor kits someone out with cloth and trims the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip or make ready, as in getting a room ready, is a sense of the verb.

clue.text: Reporters offering similarity for the listeners

indicators.note: listeners hear rather than read, so this signals a word that sounds alike

parts.note: correspondence means likeness or matching

explanation.surface: Journalists bringing listeners a likeness of events.
explanation.definitionFit: News journalists covering a beat or a foreign posting are reporters by title.

clue.text: Map includes one stretch of level land

indicators.note: includes means the map word holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chart showing a flat expanse of country.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide flat area of ground, such as a prairie, is a common geographical term.

clue.text: Special song that man heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is identified by sound alone

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A special tune that a fellow listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise sung in church worship is a sacred, special piece.

clue.text: This person having chat with sailor is an A-list celeb

parts.note: this person is the speaker, me
gas is idle talk
tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: Someone chatting with a sailor turns out to be a big star.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely famous performer or celebrity at the very top of the A list.

clue.text: In big town there's a very small space

indicators.note: In places the article and the abbreviation inside the town word

parts.note: a city is a big town

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a large town there is a tiny gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow or hole, as in a tooth, is a small enclosed space.

clue.text: What's played esp. in inn?

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved around in play

parts.note: the abbreviation esp. gives its three letters
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub game, especially one played in a tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges ESP, IN and INN; the whole clue also describes the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles with nine pins, a traditional pub game in which a ball knocks down pins.

clue.text: Disloyalty with leader doing a bunk — motive?

indicators.note: doing a bunk is running off, so the first letter of the disloyalty word leaves

parts.note: treason is disloyalty to one's country

explanation.surface: A traitor's chief flees, leaving the question of why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a bunk' is British slang for running away; it removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause or ground for doing something is a motive, a direct synonym.
